rounds.text: Rajputana Biodiesel trades at an attractive P/E multiple of 27.8x compared to a sector benchmark of 68.77x [E1, E6], offering significant relative value alongside a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 286 per share that provides a substantial margin of safety of 31.8% [E36, E37]. The underlying business has demonstrated exceptional historical expansion, evidenced by 5-year compounded sales growth of 44% and 5-year profit growth of 41% [E12, E15]. Growth catalysts are firmly in place through a massive expansion in production capacity to 130-150 kilolitres per day starting from the coming financial year, alongside successful enhancements of 3 to 4 times at the Phulera and Meerut units [E64, E74]. Furthermore, the company is actively capitalizing on massive industry tailwinds, including the National Biofuels Policy's 5% domestic blending target, high-volume OMC tenders with long-term supply contracts, and new high-margin verticals such as compressed biogas and European and GCC marine blending markets [E66, E69, E70, E73, E75]. Conceded: operating cash flow turned negative to Rs -0.67 Cr in Mar 2026, borrowings increased to Rs 22.92 Cr, institutional ownership has seen outflows, and operating margins have compressed over the last four years [E23, E26, E30, E34, E35].

Despite reported revenue growth, Rajputana Biodiesel Ltd exhibits severe operational and financial deterioration that undermines its valuation and investment case [E52]. Operating margins have steadily contracted by 4 percentage points over the last three years to 11% in March 2026, driven by a consistent downward yearly trend [E21, E23]. Most alarmingly, cash generation has completely collapsed: operating cash flow turned deeply negative at Rs -0.67 Cr and free cash flow plummeted to Rs -2.33 Cr in March 2026, yielding a dismal cash conversion ratio of -0.14x [E25, E26, E27]. This cash burn has forced the company to ramp up borrowings to Rs 22.92 Cr, nearly doubling its debt load from a year prior [E30]. Concurrently, institutional investors have fled in a clear vote of no confidence, with foreign and domestic institutional holdings plunging by 3.39 percentage points and 8.18 percentage points respectively since December 2024 [E33, E34]. Furthermore, the stock languishes below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a weak relative strength rating of 32, while earnings quality is artificially flattered by Rs 2.25 Cr of other income [E41, E42, E51]. Conceded: the company boasts long-term supply contracts with major OMCs, strong historical multi-year sales growth, and ambitious capacity expansion plans [E12, E73, E75].

Conceded: the company trades at a P/E of 27.8x against a sector benchmark of 68.77x [E1, E6]. However, this relative multiple discount is entirely justified by the deteriorating cash generation and institutional flight that the bull attempts to gloss over [E25, E35]. While the bull celebrates historic 5-year sales and profit growth [E12, E15], current results show that net profit contracted by 7% year-on-year, earnings growth is actively decelerating, and operating margins have compressed over the last four years [E23, E55, E56]. The touted capacity expansion to 130-150 kilolitres per day and new project timelines [E64, E69, E70] coincide with a surge in capital work-in-progress up 125.3% and a spike in borrowings to Rs 22.92 Cr [E30, E31], while operating cash flow collapsed to a negative Rs -0.67 Cr in March 2026 [E26]. Finally, the institutional confidence the bull implies is directly contradicted by heavy domestic and foreign institutional outflows, pushing institutional holding down to a meager 2.65% and triggering negative money flow signals [E33, E34, E35].

Conceded: the company trades at a P/E multiple of 27.8x versus a sector benchmark of 68.77x and exhibits 5-year compounded sales and profit growth of 44% and 41% respectively [E1, E6, E12, E15]. However, this relative valuation ignores severe fundamental deterioration, as operating margins have compressed over the last four years and dropped to 11% by March 2026 alongside negative cash conversion of -0.14x [E21, E23, E25]. While capacity enhancements and new verticals are cited as growth catalysts [E64, E70, E74], these capital-intensive plans have triggered a surge in borrowings to Rs 22.92 Cr and pushed operating cash flow into a deficit of Rs -0.67 Cr along with a negative free cash flow of Rs -2.33 Cr in March 2026 [E26, E27, E30]. Conceded: management highlights long-term OMC supply contracts and biofuels policy targets [E66, E75]. Yet institutional investors have heavily exited the stock, with domestic and foreign institutional holdings plummeting drastically between December 2024 and March 2026 and driving a negative money flow signal [E33, E34, E35]. Finally, the stock price sits well below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a negative 12-month return of -25.1%, confirming that technical momentum completely rejects the bull thesis [E41, E43].
